title: Leaf-Similar Trees
prompt:
Consider all the leaf nodes of a binary tree, from left to right, forming a sequence of leaf values called the tree's leaf value sequence. Given the roots of two binary trees `root1` and `root2`, return `true` if and only if the two trees have the same leaf value sequence.

Both trees are given as level-order arrays where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives both arrays directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds a tree from an array, so you only need to compare the leaf sequences.

examples.explanation: Both trees produce the leaf sequence [6,7,4,9,8] when read left to right.
root1's leaves in order are [2,3]; root2's leaves in order are [3,2] — different sequences.

constraints: The number of nodes in each tree is in the range [1, 200]
hints: You don't need to build the full tree structures to compare — just extract the sequence of leaf values from each tree via a left-to-right DFS.
A node is a leaf if it has no left and no right child; collect its value into a list only when this is true.
Once you have both leaf sequences, the trees are leaf-similar exactly when the two lists are equal element-for-element.

solution.approach: Run a DFS (preferring left before right, so the order matches left-to-right reading) on each tree, collecting the value of every node with no children into a list. Two trees are leaf-similar exactly when these two leaf sequences are identical.
